ch1.title: Navigation & Directory Listing
ch1.subtitle: Locate yourself, inspect hidden files, browse directory trees, and use Tab completion
ch1.intro: Every Linux session starts with knowing where you are, seeing what lives around you, and moving between directories efficiently. In this chapter you'll practice pwd, ls, tree, and cd—and let Tab do the heavy typing.
ch1.goal.1: Run pwd to print the absolute path of your current working directory
ch1.goal.2: Run ls -a or ls -la to inspect hidden files (discover .hidden_note)
ch1.goal.3: Run tree to view the directory hierarchy
ch1.goal.4: Use cd (try Tab completion!) to enter workspace/long-directory-name-for-tab-practice
ch1.hint.1: Run pwd to print your current path, and run ls -la to view detailed file listings including dotfiles starting with '.'.
ch1.hint.2: Run tree to display a visual hierarchy of files and subdirectories.
ch1.hint.3: Type 'cd workspace/long' and press Tab—the shell will autocomplete it to 'cd workspace/long-directory-name-for-tab-practice'. Press Enter to move in.
ch1.softlock: The practice directories or hidden files for this chapter were altered, which may prevent verification.
ch2.title: File & Directory Management
ch2.subtitle: Create nested folders, touch files, move/rename, copy recursively, remove, and symlink
ch2.intro: Organizing project layouts, backing up directories, cleaning temporary files, and creating symbolic links are everyday Linux essentials. Follow the objectives below to tidy up your workspace.
ch2.goal.1: Create the nested directory lab/docs/archive using mkdir -p
ch2.goal.2: Create an empty file at lab/notes.md using touch
ch2.goal.3: Move and rename inbox/report_draft.txt to lab/docs/report.txt using mv
ch2.goal.4: Recursively copy templates to lab/templates_backup (cp -r) and remove inbox/junk.tmp (rm)
ch2.goal.5: Create a symbolic link lab/current_report pointing to docs/report.txt (relative to lab/) or /home/learner/lab/docs/report.txt with ln -s
ch2.hint.1: Use 'mkdir -p lab/docs/archive' to create all missing parent directories at once, then run 'touch lab/notes.md'.
ch2.hint.2: Use 'mv inbox/report_draft.txt lab/docs/report.txt' to move and rename, 'cp -r templates lab/templates_backup' to copy a directory, and 'rm inbox/junk.tmp' to delete the temporary file.
ch2.hint.3: Symbolic link syntax is 'ln -s <target> <link_name>', e.g., 'ln -s docs/report.txt lab/current_report' (or 'ln -s /home/learner/lab/docs/report.txt lab/current_report').
ch2.softlock: Required source files (inbox/report_draft.txt or templates) are missing or modified.
ch3.title: Viewing, Paging & Editing Text
ch3.subtitle: Inspect logs with head, tail, wc, and less, then edit configs in nano
ch3.intro: Reading server logs and tweaking configuration files directly in the terminal is a core daily skill. Start by previewing and counting lines in a log file, browse it interactively with less, and then update a config file with nano.
ch3.goal.1: Inspect the start or end of logs/server.log using head or tail
ch3.goal.2: Count the total number of lines in logs/server.log using wc -l
ch3.goal.3: Open logs/server.log in less (scroll with j/k or arrows, search with /TOKEN, quit with q)
ch3.goal.4: Edit app.conf with nano (Ctrl+O to save, Ctrl+X to exit) so that debug=false and port=9000
ch3.hint.1: Try 'head -n 10 logs/server.log' or 'tail -n 10 logs/server.log' to inspect lines, and 'wc -l logs/server.log' to count total lines.
ch3.hint.2: Run 'less logs/server.log' to open the pager: scroll with j/k or arrow keys, type '/TOKEN' and press Enter to search, and press 'q' when done.
ch3.hint.3: Run 'nano app.conf', change debug=true to debug=false and port=8080 to port=9000, press Ctrl+O then Enter to save, and Ctrl+X to exit.
ch3.softlock: logs/server.log or app.conf is missing and cannot be inspected or edited.
ch4.title: Search & Text Processing
ch4.subtitle: Locate files with find, search text with grep, and slice/deduplicate data with cut, sort, and uniq
ch4.intro: When working with large codebases and structured text files, manual browsing doesn't scale. Practice combining Linux's classic search and text-processing utilities to find files, grep for errors, and clean CSV data.
ch4.goal.1: Use find to locate all .yaml files under src
ch4.goal.2: Use grep -r (or grep -rn) to recursively search for ERROR inside src
ch4.goal.3: Extract the first column (usernames) from data/users.csv using cut -d , -f 1
ch4.goal.4: Deduplicate data/users.csv using sort and uniq (e.g., sort data/users.csv | uniq)
ch4.hint.1: Search by filename pattern: find src -name '*.yaml' (quote the pattern so the shell doesn't expand '*' prematurely).
ch4.hint.2: Search recursively inside a directory: grep -rn ERROR src (-r for recursive, -n to show line numbers).
ch4.hint.3: Extract column 1 with comma delimiter: cut -d , -f 1 data/users.csv. Because uniq only collapses adjacent duplicates, sort first: sort data/users.csv | uniq.
ch4.softlock: The src directory or data/users.csv file is missing, so search and processing objectives cannot be verified.
ch5.title: Pipes, Redirections & Chaining
ch5.subtitle: Compose commands into pipelines with |, >, >>, wildcards *, and conditional &&
ch5.intro: The real power of the Unix philosophy lies in composition: pass output between commands with pipes (|), save or append results with > and >>, match batches of files with *, and chain dependent steps with &&.
ch5.goal.1: Filter ERROR lines from events/app.log, sort and deduplicate them via pipes (|), and redirect (>) into errors.txt
ch5.goal.2: Append (>>) the line '--- END ---' to errors.txt
ch5.goal.3: Use the wildcard * with cat and > to combine events/notes_*.txt into combined.txt
ch5.goal.4: Use && chaining to create directory done_dir and file done_dir/ok.txt in a single command line
ch5.hint.1: Chain filter, sort, deduplicate, and redirect: grep ERROR events/app.log | sort | uniq > errors.txt
ch5.hint.2: Use double angle brackets (>>) to append without overwriting: echo '--- END ---' >> errors.txt
ch5.hint.3: Combine matching files with 'cat events/notes_*.txt > combined.txt'. Chain directory and file creation with 'mkdir -p done_dir && touch done_dir/ok.txt'.
ch5.softlock: Source files under events/ are missing, preventing pipeline and merge tasks.
ch6.title: Permissions, Env & Running Scripts
ch6.subtitle: Inspect permissions with ls -l / stat, grant +x with chmod, export env vars, and run scripts
ch6.intro: New scripts in Linux aren't executable by default, and build or deployment scripts frequently rely on environment variables. In this chapter you'll inspect permissions, make a script executable, export a build flag, and run it.
ch6.goal.1: Inspect the permissions of build/compile.sh using ls -l or stat
ch6.goal.2: Add execute permission to build/compile.sh using chmod +x or chmod 755
ch6.goal.3: Export the environment variable BUILD_MODE=release using export BUILD_MODE=release
ch6.goal.4: Run ./compile.sh inside build/ (or ./build/compile.sh) to generate build/out/artifact.txt
ch6.hint.1: Run 'ls -l build/compile.sh' or 'stat build/compile.sh' to inspect its permission bits—notice the missing 'x' flag.
ch6.hint.2: Grant execute permission with 'chmod +x build/compile.sh', then export the variable with 'export BUILD_MODE=release'.
ch6.hint.3: Execute './build/compile.sh' (or 'cd build && ./compile.sh'), and inspect build/out/artifact.txt to confirm the build succeeded.
ch6.softlock: build/compile.sh is missing or corrupted and can no longer be executed.
ch7.title: Archives & Build Toolchain
ch7.subtitle: Build programs with gcc / make and package or extract directories with tar and gzip
ch7.intro: Compiling software from source and packaging directories into compressed archives are foundational Linux skills. Here you'll build and run a C program using the simulated gcc/make toolchain, then archive and extract an assets folder.
ch7.goal.1: Inside project/, build project/app from src/main.c using gcc -o app src/main.c or make
ch7.goal.2: Run the compiled executable ./app inside project/
ch7.goal.3: Compress project/assets into project/assets.tar.gz using tar -czf assets.tar.gz assets
ch7.goal.4: Create /home/learner/extracted and extract project/assets.tar.gz into it
ch7.hint.1: Enter the project directory with 'cd project', compile using 'make' or 'gcc -o app src/main.c', and run './app'.
ch7.hint.2: Inside project/, compress the assets directory: tar -czf assets.tar.gz assets (c=create, z=gzip, f=archive file).
ch7.hint.3: Create the destination directory first with 'mkdir -p /home/learner/extracted', then extract using -C: tar -xzf /home/learner/project/assets.tar.gz -C /home/learner/extracted
ch7.softlock: project/src/main.c, Makefile, or project/assets is missing, preventing build and archive tasks.
ch8.title: Capstone Integration Challenge
ch8.subtitle: Combine everything you learned: log triage, config editing, script build, verification, and release packaging
ch8.intro: Welcome to the final capstone! Inside release_prep sits a service waiting to be prepared for release. Bring together log filtering, text editing, permissions, script execution, and tar archiving to complete the end-to-end release workflow.
ch8.goal.1: Extract all CRITICAL lines from release_prep/logs/deploy.log into release_prep/critical.txt
ch8.goal.2: Update release_prep/config/env.conf so ENV=staging is changed to ENV=prod
ch8.goal.3: Grant execute permission to release_prep/scripts/compile.sh and run it to build release_prep/dist/service
ch8.goal.4: Run release_prep/dist/service to verify the compiled service output
ch8.hint.1: Start with 'tree release_prep' to orient yourself, then extract critical logs: grep CRITICAL release_prep/logs/deploy.log > release_prep/critical.txt
ch8.hint.2: Open the config with 'nano release_prep/config/env.conf', change ENV=staging to ENV=prod, press Ctrl+O then Enter to save, and Ctrl+X to exit.
ch8.hint.3: Make the build script executable and run it: chmod +x release_prep/scripts/compile.sh && ./release_prep/scripts/compile.sh, then run ./release_prep/dist/service.
ch8.hint.4: Package the dist directory: tar -czf /home/learner/release_v2.tar.gz -C release_prep dist (or 'cd release_prep && tar -czf /home/learner/release_v2.tar.gz dist').
ch8.softlock: Critical source files under release_prep (logs, config, or build script) are missing.
sandbox.title: Free Practice Sandbox
sandbox.subtitle: An open virtual Linux playground with no limits
sandbox.intro: There are no objectives or grading here—create files, chain pipelines, test permissions, practice tar archives, or try out examples from 'man'. Run 'reset' to refresh the sandbox, or 'chapter <1-8>' to switch back to a lesson.
